name: tower-block-sub-boom
idea: This is the closest answer to Kai's pick: the 1994 hardstep he chose with the detuned-saw growl bass torn out and nothing growling in its place. The lead voice is one enormous clean sub-bass boom, a deep pitched-down kick-drum hum that drops and slides on every bar so the floor shakes. Above it, the Amen hits raw and almost unedited, with a hard kick doubled underneath. Ask for it as a short front-loaded tag list that names hardstep jungle and the Amen in the first words, then sub-bass weight, 165 BPM, instrumental and no intro. Push weirdness to about 55 with style influence high (about 80) so it stays in the lane but finds a stranger groove than last round.

name: rooftop-pirate-transmission
idea: Ask for it as a broadcast: a Sunday-night jungle pirate set coming off an aerial on a 21-storey council tower block, caught on a cheap kitchen radio. Here the lead voice is the drums. The Amen does all the talking: chopped, edited and rolling hard, smashing cymbals to one side. Under it runs a reversed sub-bass line that swells backwards into each downbeat (the 1994 trick), with no midrange bass at all. Write it as a vivid prose scene, with FM hiss and signal drift as the only texture and nothing melodic. Set weirdness to about 65 and style influence to about 65.

name: concrete-stairwell-distortion
idea: Make it the sound of the estate itself, heard from inside the concrete. The lead voice is a deliberately distorted, overdriven sub bass, creeping and predatory, that rattles the windows and buzzes the metal stair rails. The distortion is on the sub itself, the mid-90s dark heavyweight kind, not two detuned saw basses. The Amen sounds as if it is being played in a bare concrete stairwell: hard, menacing smacks with a short, hard slapback off the walls. It should be aggressive and industrial, with barely any respite. Ask for it through texture and materials words (concrete, steel shutters, lift shaft, cold strip light) placed after the genre words, not through a tag list. Set weirdness to about 75 and style influence to about 70.

name: sampler-mangled-amen
idea: Ask for it as technique and equipment, not mood: a bedroom-studio 12-bit sampler jungle tool from 1994 or 1995. The lead voice is the timestretched, multi-pitched Amen itself, mangled into robotic stutters, pitched up and down, then snapped back to the raw loop, so it feels cyborg-like. The bass is a single pitched-down sine sub sampled off the same machine, gritty, aliased and lo-fi, playing a blunt two-note figure. Keep the prompt to a terse list of production terms (timestretched Amen, 12-bit grit, sine sub, dubplate mastering, 165 BPM, instrumental, no intro). This is the wildest of the four, with weirdness at about 80 and style influence at about 60, and it should still hit from the first beat and loop cleanly.
